title: scan.rs is_begin_line requires 'begin ' (with space) but decode.rs matches bare 'begin' — divergent begin-line detection
description: uuencoding/src/scan.rs is_begin_line() (line 50) requires the line to start with 'begin ' (6 chars including space) and rejects 'begin' alone. uuencoding/src/decode.rs looks for any line where the lowercased version starts_with(b'begin') (line 29), which includes 'begin\n'. These two entry points diverge on edge inputs. A bare 'begin\n' block would be found by decode() (returning mode=0, filename='') but skipped by scan(). This is a latent user-confusion bug: calling decode() on a slice discovered by scan() is safe, but calling scan() to detect if a body has blocks, then decode() on the whole body, will disagree on membership.
acceptance_criteria: Unify begin-line detection into one shared function used by both decode.rs and scan.rs. The canonical behavior should be documented clearly.
close_reason: is_begin_line now accepts bare begin (no trailing space); parse_begin_line handles bare begin with defaults; added test
